exposure: Socio-demographic factors (educational status, employment status, gravidity)
outcome: Attitude towards elective repeat caesarean delivery
cohort: The study included 334 pregnant women attending an antenatal clinic at a tertiary care hospital in Rawalpindi.
finding: Pregnant women showed better knowledge of vaginal delivery than caesarean delivery, but a significant majority had a positive attitude towards primary caesarean delivery primarily due to fear of labor pains.
mod_finding: The study found that pregnant women had better knowledge of vaginal delivery compared to caesarean section but displayed a positive attitude towards primary caesarean delivery due to fear of labor pains, and also fear of pain during and after surgery for vaginal birth after caesarean.
